EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Cheap operating earnings are less attractive if short-term obligations are building faster than the revenue base. A falling current-liability burden indicates improving operating financing pressure, so the signal distinguishes cheap EBITDA from near-term balance-sheet stress.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Signed Working-Capital Book Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), revt), 1), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: High book-to-market firms should outperform when book cheapness is not accompanied by rising net working-capital intensity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This directly repairs the prior working-capital stability failure by using the signed buildup rather than the absolute change. Rising net working capital relative to revenue can indicate receivables or inventory accumulation, so cheap book equity is penalized when accounting capital is expanding without clear cash realization.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Maintenance-Light Cash Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dp, revt), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash-rich value firms should be more attractive when depreciation burden is low relative to revenue.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Cash on the balance sheet is more likely to represent distributable or protective value when the business does not require heavy asset replacement. This avoids mechanically turning EBITDA into EBIT, instead asking whether cash-to-market cheapness is safer in businesses with lower maintenance-capital pressure.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Gross-Profit Claim Covered Cashflow Yield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), lct), 1)))

REASONING: The earlier sales-value gross-margin signal had positive Fama-MacBeth evidence but negative FF5 alpha, suggesting cheap sales alone may load into distressed low-quality portfolios. This version requires cash-flow yield as the valuation anchor and uses gross-profit claim coverage to identify firms whose operating economics can support near-term obligations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
